question.text: Can Ambu self-inflating bag and Neopuff infant resuscitator provide adequate and safe manual inflations for infants up to 10 kg weight?
question.context: Manual resuscitation devices for infants and newborns must be able to provide adequate ventilation in a safe and consistent manner across a wide range of patient sizes (0.5-10 kg) and differing clinical states. There are little comparative data assessing biomechanical performance of common infant manual resuscitation devices across the manufacturers' recommended operating weight ranges. We aimed to compare performance of the Ambu self-inflating bag (SIB) with the Neopuff T-piece resuscitator in three resuscitation models. Five experienced clinicians delivered targeted ventilation to three lung models differing in compliance, delivery pressures and inflation rates; Preterm (0.5 mL/cmH2O, 25/5 cmH2O, 60 per minute), Term (3 mL/cmH2O, 30/5 cmH2O, 40 per minute) and Infant (9 mL/cmH2O, 35/5 cmH2O, 30 per minute). The Neopuff was examined with three gas inflow rates (5 litres per minute (LPM), 10 LPM and 15 LPM) and the Ambu with no gas inflow. 3309 inflations were collected and analysed with analysis of variance for repeated measures. The Neopuff was unable to reach set peak inflation pressures and exhibited seriously elevated positive end expiratory pressure (PEEP) with all inflow gas rates (p<0.001) in this infant model. The Ambu SIB accurately delivered targeted pressures in all three models.

medgemma_4b.clinical_reasoning: The study compared the Ambu self-inflating bag and Neopuff resuscitator in infant resuscitation models. The Ambu SIB accurately delivered targeted pressures in all three models, while the Neopuff exhibited elevated PEEP and failed to reach set peak inflation pressures. This indicates the Ambu SIB is a more reliable and safe option for manual inflations in infants up to 10 kg.
medgemma_4b.critical_evidence: The Ambu SIB accurately delivered targeted pressures in all three models, while the Neopuff exhibited elevated PEEP and failed to reach set peak inflation pressures.
medgemma_4b.differential_considered: While the study focused on the Ambu SIB and Neopuff, other manual resuscitation devices could potentially be used. However, the study's findings strongly suggest that the Ambu SIB is a more reliable and safe option for manual inflations in infants up to 10 kg, making it the best answer.

rnj1_8b.clinical_reasoning: The study found that the Ambu SIB accurately delivered targeted pressures in all three models, while the Neopuff failed to reach set peak inflation pressures and showed elevated PEEP in the infant model. This indicates the Ambu SIB provides adequate and safe manual inflations for infants up to 10 kg, but the Neopuff does not meet the safety and performance requirements for this age group.
rnj1_8b.critical_evidence: The Neopuff's inability to reach set peak inflation pressures and elevated PEEP in the infant model demonstrates it cannot provide safe manual inflations for infants up to 10 kg.
rnj1_8b.differential_considered: No differential diagnoses needed - this is a device performance question. The key consideration was the comparative performance of the two devices, with the Ambu SIB showing consistent performance across all models while the Neopuff failed in the infant model.

qwen3_vl_8b.clinical_reasoning: The Ambu self-inflating bag accurately delivered targeted pressures across all three lung models (preterm, term, infant), whereas the Neopuff failed to reach set pressures and exhibited dangerously elevated PEEP. This demonstrates the Ambu SIB’s superior performance for safe and adequate ventilation in infants up to 10 kg.
qwen3_vl_8b.critical_evidence: The Ambu SIB accurately delivered targeted pressures in all three models, while the Neopuff failed to meet targets and showed elevated PEEP (p<0.001) in the infant model.
qwen3_vl_8b.differential_considered: Neopuff’s performance was considered a differential, but it was ruled out due to its inability to deliver adequate pressures and safety concerns, making Ambu the only viable option based on the data.

olmo3_7b.differential_considered: The Neopuff's inability to achieve target pressures and high PEEP raises concerns about its safety and efficacy, especially in challenging resuscitation scenarios. Other manual resuscitators (e.g., Manikat, Laryngoscope-guided bag mask) were not evaluated here, but the direct comparison shows the Ambu SIB is superior in pressure delivery for the tested range.
